Safe habits for floor markings on the job
Trainers ask staff to read this twice, and this page helps new colleagues see why

At the Companion Animal Travel Desk of Aurelia Skyways, floor markings are part of safe movement, calm service, and clear handoff work. I am sorry to say that when we rush or ignore the markers, the whole path for passengers, carriers, and staff becomes harder to manage. Please treat each line, sign, and queue space as a guide for where to stand, where to place a carrier, and where to wait for the next handoff.

Use the markings to keep travel lanes open and to separate customer space from the working area. A carrier should never block a marked path, and no one should step over a barrier line unless the task calls for it. When you guide a traveler with a pet, speak in a steady voice and keep your own pace unhurried. Calm handling helps the animal stay settled, and it helps us avoid sudden shifts that can upset nearby passengers.

When a pet and crate come to the desk, check the carrier position against the marked area before anything else. <<FACT F073>> Then continue with the usual care steps and watch for signs that the crate needs to be moved or steadied. <<FACT F061>> If the marked area is crowded, ask the ground team for help rather than trying to squeeze past with a pet in hand.

If a traveler arrives with Bailey or another animal, keep your tone warm and plain. We do not hurry people through this process, and we do not make a scene if something needs to be adjusted. Instead, we reset the space, confirm the route, and keep the desk clear for the next person. This is one of the simplest ways to show respect and reduce stress for everyone nearby.

Remember that floor markings are not decoration; they are part of safe service, and we rely on you to follow them carefully on every shift.
